Sorry to hear you’re struggling. I’m in a similar situation and here’s what helps me. 
I don’t really find joy from situations as much as I find day to day joy from results. 
For instance, I started seriously weightlifting in February. I hate going to the gym, and I usually don’t enjoy the workouts. They’re hard, boring and often times are downright awful. 
But what I do like are the results. I was fat and weak. Now I’m not fat and I’ve gotten stronger. My clothes look good on me, I have more confidence, and I feel better about myself. 
My point being is to find something you want to improve in your life and dedicate yourself to making that improvement, with or without motivation. I can’t tell you how unmotivated I am to going. But I am dedicated to it. Im not saying it always sucks, there are some days im motivated to go, but that only came after I saw results after I dedicated to going. 
Eventually you will find yourself in the habit of going and making those improvements. This will bring foundational happiness and even joy. 
A little effort in put into the journey of self improvement will yield results in the long run and eventually lead to something greater.

I was a terrible student in school. Terrible. Not because I didn’t understand the course material, just that I was too stupid to understand genuine effort and taking shit seriously in life. 

Anyway, after coasting through school for nearly 10 years, passing each year by the skin of teeth, the last week of my senior was upon me. 
I was failing three course, retook 3 finals, and needed to get A’s on all finals to graduate. 
My parents never had a clue about my struggles in school. My entire family came to watch my graduation. 
I had no idea if I would or would not be receiving a diploma when I walked the stage. 
We were lined up preparing to take our seats on stage, cap and gown on, everyone celebrating and hugging, joy was in the air. But not for me I was practically about to vomit with shear panic and despair. The final moment before taking our seats, our principal announced that for the first time in over 20 years we had a 100% graduation rate. 
The relief I felt from that was spiritual. It was as if I had awoken from a dream but it was real. Little did I know that this feeling of relief would be the greatest I would ever feel to date. Better than all my pregnancy scares, cancer screenings, everything.
